findings.title: Difficulty curve is flat: every tier, clumsy included, clears levels 1-100 with 3 stars
findings.detail: All 35 tier-level runs were cleared on the first attempt; 34 of them earned 3 stars. Clumsy (650 ms reaction, 40 px noise, 500 css px/s strokes, random nozzle choice) cleared level 100 in 218 s (time limit 358 s, 3-star par 310 s). Superhuman cleared level 100 in 41 s (13% of par) and level 99 in 21 s. par and limitVal come from est (index.html:582-584), which assumes one slow sweep at vW px/s with an 80 px swath. Back-and-forth scrubbing at ordinary finger speed beats that estimate by 2-7x, so the 3-star target and the time/water limits never bind and level 100 is not much harder than level 1.
findings.repro: node qa/skill-tiers/pressure-washer/bot.js clumsy  (LV=100 for one level). See results.json tiers.*.summary.
findings.fix: Calibrate par/budget against a fast-scrub reference (e.g. measure a bot like world tier), or make est use the real per-pass removal model; tighten L.budget/starMul for k>20.

findings.title: Spray strength depends on frame rate and stroke speed (normalisation clamp)
findings.detail: In spray() (index.html:659) each stamp gets alpha ag*f with f = clamp(1.6/cnt, 0.4, 1), where cnt = stamps per frame. Grime removed per second of spraying therefore depends on how many pixels the finger covers per frame: with cnt>=2 a frame removes 1.6x (up to 0.4*cnt x) the cnt=1 amount. Fast strokes clean more per second than slow ones (6 identical passes on L50: 300 css px/s gives 1.35 %/s, 1500 css px/s gives 2.5 %/s). The same stroke also cleans differently at different refresh rates: at 1500 css px/s, 30 fps cleaned 4.04%, 60 fps 3.75%, 120 fps 0%, because at 120 fps cnt stays 1 and no cell crossed the alpha>40 threshold. In a full L50 run with the same world policy at 900 css px/s, 30 fps cleared in 106 s but 60 fps failed with 69.5% at the 292 s limit. Players on 120 Hz phones get a noticeably weaker washer.
findings.repro: Level 50; hold a finger at the stage middle row and swipe 6 passes across at 1500 css px/s; compare % at 30/60/120 fps (experiments.microStroke_L50_6passes_one_lane in results.json).
findings.fix: Make per-stamp strength proportional to dt/cnt (f = 1/cnt) so the dose per point depends only on the time it spends under the nozzle, then retune NOZ grime/mud constants (and par) once.

findings.title: Careful play is not rewarded: scrubbing speed dominates and skill barely changes the result
findings.detail: Mean cleaning rate (% per minute): clumsy 52.7, casual 80.9, skilled 66.5, world 94.6, superhuman 182.3. The careful skilled bot (re-checks each lane) was slower than the careless casual one; on level 75 it got 2 stars, the only non-3-star result. The only skill that pays is stroke speed, which ties to the clamp above.
findings.fix: Covered by the two fixes above.

findings.title: Robustness: clumsy input caused no errors
findings.detail: Across 7 clumsy runs there were 97 injected events (second finger while spraying, 6 rapid taps, rotating to 844x390 and back with the finger down, backgrounding 2 s with the finger down) and no page or console errors, stuck spray or dropped pointers. Pausing elapsed time while hidden works (frame() returns while document.hidden). Bots saw 7 nozzle taps not register, but a dedicated 8-case retest (drag or tap then nozzle tap, gaps 0-400 ms) did not reproduce it; treated as a harness artefact of pipelined CDP input.
